% --- Resumo (PT) e Abstract (EN) ---
\begin{resumo}
A proliferação exponencial da Internet das Coisas (IoT) produziu uma vasta
superfície de ataque enquanto as restrições computacionais de muitos dispositivos
tornam ineficazes as soluções tradicionais, motivando mecanismos de defesa
adaptativos e autônomos. Esta dissertação projeta, implementa e avalia um
arcabouço de defesa adaptativo ciente da cadeia de eliminação cibernética
(\emph{kill-chain-aware}) para redes IoT, baseado em Aprendizado por Reforço
Profundo (DRL) e avaliado a partir de linhas de características reais do
\emph{dataset} CICIoT2023 amostradas em uma trajetória de \emph{kill chain}
simulada sobre cinco estágios. O adversário reage à força do defensor num
\emph{cabo de guerra} sobre a cadeia. De forma central, a defesa é formulada
como um problema genuíno de \emph{observabilidade parcial}: o defensor nunca
observa o verdadeiro estágio, de modo que este só pode ser inferido ao longo de
uma janela temporal. Treinamos agentes de RL com janela (PPO e A2C, com DQN
como \emph{baseline} \emph{off-policy}) e os comparamos a uma Floresta
Aleatória acoplada a detector (RF-Acting), a um oráculo de observabilidade
total e a políticas triviais. Três resultados sustentam a contribução: (i) à
medida que a ambiguidade da observação aumenta, o classificador por fluxo
degrada monotonicamente enquanto o PPO permanece estável, empatando no regime
sem ambiguidade e superando a RF com intervalos de confiança disjuntos a
partir do ponto de operação principal; (ii) uma ablação de recompensa mostra
que o melhor agente de RL supera a RF em ambos os regimes, refutando a objeção
de informação privilegiada; (iii) sob distribuição deslocada (dez classes de
ataque retidas), o melhor agente de RL com janela previne uma fração maior de
ataques em todas as classes, sem dependência detectável da acurácia do
detector. Ambos os algoritmos \emph{on-policy} (PPO e A2C) treinam de forma
confiável sob a recompensa esparsa, com desvio-padrão entre sementes
substancialmente menor que o do DQN, e o A2C
atinge o maior retorno de \emph{best-checkpoint} na taxa de \emph{aliasing}
principal; o DQN \emph{off-policy}, sem modelagem por etapa, degrada-se a
retorno negativo com variância várias vezes maior, de modo que a vantagem
\emph{on-policy} é de estabilidade de treinamento, não de retorno máximo.
Todos os resultados são acompanhados de intervalos de confiança por
\emph{bootstrap} e de uma cadeia de artefatos reprodutível.

    \vspace{\onelineskip}

    \noindent\textbf{Palavras-chave}: Segurança IoT; Aprendizado por Reforço Profundo;
    Cyber Kill Chain; Observabilidade Parcial (POMDP); \emph{Aliasing} de Observação;
    Robustez a Distribuição Deslocada; CICIoT2023; Reprodutibilidade.

    \vspace{\onelineskip}
    \vspace{\onelineskip}

    \clearpage

    \begin{otherlanguage*}{english}
    \begin{center}{\ABNTEXchapterfont\huge Abstract}\end{center}

The exponential proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT) has produced a
vast attack surface while the computational constraints of many devices render
traditional security solutions ineffective, motivating adaptive, autonomous
defense mechanisms. This dissertation designs, implements, and evaluates a
kill-chain-aware adaptive defense framework for IoT networks, built on Deep
Reinforcement Learning (DRL) and evaluated on real CICIoT2023 feature rows
sampled into a simulated kill-chain trajectory over five stages. The adversary
reacts to defender force in a \emph{tug-of-war} on the kill chain. Centrally,
the defense is cast as a genuine \emph{partially observable} problem: the
defender never observes the true stage, so the stage can be inferred only across
a temporal window. We train windowed RL agents (PPO and A2C, with DQN as an
off-policy baseline) and compare them against a detector-coupled
Random-Forest policy (RF-Acting), a full-observability oracle, and trivial
baselines. Three results support the contribution: (i) as observation
ambiguity rises the per-flow classifier degrades monotonically while windowed
PPO stays flat, tying in the unaliased regime and beating RF with disjoint
confidence intervals from the headline operating point onward; (ii) a reward
ablation shows the best RL agent beats RF-Acting under both reward regimes,
refuting the privileged-reward objection; (iii) under distribution shift
(ten held-out attack classes), the best windowed RL agent prevents a larger
fraction of attacks on every class, with no detectable dependence on detector
accuracy. Both on-policy algorithms (PPO and A2C) train reliably under the
sparse outcome reward, with substantially lower across-seed variability than
DQN, and A2C reaches the highest
best-checkpoint outcome reward at the headline aliasing rate; the off-policy
DQN --- without per-step shaping --- destabilizes, with several times the
across-seed variance, so the on-policy advantage is one of
training-time stability rather than achievable peak return. All results carry
bootstrap confidence intervals and a reproducible artifact chain.

    \vspace{\onelineskip}

    \noindent\textbf{Keywords}: IoT security; Deep Reinforcement Learning; Cyber
    Kill Chain; Partial Observability (POMDP); Observation Aliasing;
    Out-of-Distribution Robustness; CICIoT2023; Reproducibility.

    \end{otherlanguage*}
\end{resumo}

% --- Lista de simbolos ---
\begin{simbolos}
  \item[$\alpha$]                 Observation-aliasing rate (probability a step emits a feature row from a stage adjacent to the true one)
  \item[$\beta$]                  Benign false-positive-rate penalty coefficient (disabled by default)
  \item[$\gamma$]                 Discount factor
  \item[$\epsilon$]               PPO clipping parameter (also DQN exploration coefficient)
  \item[$\kappa$]                 Action-cost scale
  \item[$\lambda$]                Attacker proximity to the impact stage ($\lambda = s/4$)
  \item[$\lambda_{\text{GAE}}$]   Generalized Advantage Estimation parameter
  \item[$\pi$]                    Policy mapping states to a distribution over actions
  \item[$\pi_{\theta}$]           Parameterized policy with parameters $\theta$
  \item[$\rho$]                   Spearman rank-correlation coefficient
  \item[$\sigma_{\min}$]          Residual escalation floor (proximity-coupled escalation)
  \item[$\theta$]                 Policy / Q-network parameters
  \item[$\theta^{-}$]             Target-network parameters (DQN)
  \item[$\tau$]                   Episode trajectory $\tau = (o_1, a_1, r_1, \dots, o_T, a_T, r_T)$
  \item[$\phi$]                   Feature-extraction map $s_t \mapsto o_t \in \mathbb{R}^{290}$
  \item[$A$]                      Action set $\{\textsc{observe},\textsc{log},\textsc{restrict},\textsc{block},\textsc{isolate}\} = \{0,1,2,3,4\}$
  \item[$A_t$]                    Action random variable at step $t$
  \item[$\hat{A}_t$]              Estimated advantage at step $t$ (PPO)
  \item[$a'$]                     Next action (Bellman backup)
  \item[$b(s)$]                   Belief state: posterior distribution over latent states given the observation history
  \item[$b_{\text{prevent}}$]     Prevention bonus ($+50$)
  \item[$b_{\text{success}}$]     Terminal defense-success bonus ($+250$)
  \item[$b_{\text{deesc-cap}}$]   Per-episode cap on cumulative de-escalation reward ($+150$)
  \item[$b_{\text{prop-cap}}$]    Per-episode cap on cumulative proportionality bonus ($+100$)
  \item[$C_{\mathrm{action}}(a)$] Action-cost vector (per-action availability cost)
  \item[$c_v$]                  Value-loss coefficient (A2C, PPO critic term)
  \item[$\mathcal{D}$]            Experience-replay buffer (DQN)
  \item[$d_t$]                    Signed force gap, $d_t = a_t - \mathit{rec}(s_t)$
  \item[$\mathbb{E}$]             Expectation operator
  \item[$\hat{\mathbb{E}}_t$]     Empirical (per-step) expectation (PPO)
  \item[$H(\pi_{\theta})$]      Policy entropy regularization term (A2C, PPO)
  \item[$L(\theta)$]              DQN squared TD-error loss
  \item[$L^{\mathrm{CLIP}}(\theta)$] PPO clipped surrogate loss
  \item[$n$]                      Sample size ($n=300$ episodes per policy; $n=10$ held-out classes)
  \item[$\mathcal{O}$]            Observation space of the POMDP
  \item[$o_t$]                    Observation at step $t$; $o_t = \phi(s_t) \in \mathbb{R}^{290}$ (windowed feature stack)
  \item[$P$]                      State-transition probability function, $P(s' \mid s, a)$
  \item[$p$]                      Statistical significance ($p$-value)
  \item[$p_{\text{up}}$]          Base attacker escalation probability
  \item[$p_{\text{up}}^{\text{eff}}$] Proximity-scaled effective escalation probability
  \item[$p_{\text{down}}$]        Attacker de-escalation probability
  \item[$p_{\text{down}}^{\textsc{iso}}$] De-escalation probability when the proportionate action is \textsc{isolate}
  \item[$p_{\text{onset}}$]       Benign$\rightarrow$recon onset probability
  \item[$p_{\text{onset,access}}$] Benign$\rightarrow$access onset probability
  \item[$p_{\text{disp}}$]        Disproportionate-action penalty
  \item[$p_{\text{over}}$]        Overreact-on-benign penalty
  \item[$p_{\text{block-benign}}$] Block-on-benign penalty
  \item[$p_{\text{block-recon}}$]  Block-on-recon penalty
  \item[$p_{\text{impact}}$]      Terminal-impact penalty
  \item[$p_{\text{missed}}$]      Missed-impact penalty
  \item[$Q^{\pi}(s,a)$]           Action-value function under policy $\pi$
  \item[$Q^{*}(s,a)$]             Optimal action-value function
  \item[$R$]                      Reward function
  \item[$R_t$]                    Per-step reward (sum of the six components)
  \item[$R_{t+k+1}$]              Reward at future step $t{+}k{+}1$ (Bellman return)
  \item[$\hat{R}_t$]            Return estimate used in the A2C/PPO critic loss
  \item[$r_t(\theta)$]            PPO probability ratio between new and old policy
  \item[$\mathit{rec}(s)$]        Recommended-action mapping (stage $\rightarrow$ action)
  \item[$r_{\text{prop}}$]        Proportionality bonus
  \item[$r_{\text{benign}}$]      Benign-passive bonus
  \item[$r_{\text{deesc}}$]       De-escalation reward
  \item[$\mathcal{S}$]            Latent state space of the POMDP
  \item[$s'$]                     Next (successor) latent state
  \item[$s_t$]                    Latent kill-chain stage at decision time $t$ (hidden from the defender; accessed only by the oracle)
  \item[$s^{\text{stage}}_t$]     True (latent) kill-chain stage at step $t$
  \item[$S_t$]                    State random variable at step $t$
  \item[$V^{\pi}(s)$]             State-value function under policy $\pi$
  \item[$w$]                      History window size ($w=5$)
  \item[$Z$]                      Observation model of the POMDP, $Z(o \mid s', a)$
  \item[$\mathrm{lr}$]            Learning rate
  \item[$n_{\text{steps}}$]       On-policy rollout length (PPO, A2C)
  \item[$n_{\text{epochs}}$]      Number of PPO optimization epochs per rollout
\end{simbolos}
